title: Airport SUV Luggage: What to Confirm Before You Book
description: Prepare a clear luggage brief for an airport SUV ride: passenger count, bag dimensions, strollers and bulky items, with a copyable confirmation checklist.
cta: Plan the ride for everyone and everything traveling.
image_alt: A graphite rolling suitcase and brown leather weekender beside tall lobby windows in low morning sunlight.
body:
Before booking an airport SUV, send the passenger count and a complete luggage list together. Include the outside dimensions of large cases, the folded size of a stroller, and any equipment that cannot be folded or stacked. Ask the transportation provider to confirm the vehicle arrangement for that exact combination.

A passenger count alone does not answer the luggage question. Nor does a label such as Business SUV tell you how a particular collection of bags will load with the seats your party needs. The useful question is: can the proposed vehicle carry these passengers and these belongings in the agreed configuration?

Count every item that goes into the vehicle

Make one list for the whole party rather than collecting separate replies such as 'one suitcase each.' Include checked cases, cabin bags, backpacks, laptop bags and shopping bags. Add items that are easy to overlook: a stroller, a travel cot, golf clubs, a garment bag or a large presentation case.

Distinguish between a bag and what travels separately. If a stroller folds into one piece but its seat or accessories travel in another bag, list both. If a child restraint will be used during the ride, describe that seating requirement separately from a restraint being carried as baggage.

  • Passengers: total travelers, including children, and the child-restraint or boarding arrangements to discuss.
  • Cases: count each size and note rigid or soft construction.
  • Small bags: include personal items, even if you usually carry them on your shoulder.
  • Bulky items: list each stroller, sports bag, equipment case or other unusually shaped item separately.

Send usable measurements

For large or unusual items, measure the packed outside length, width and height, including protruding wheels, fixed handles and pockets. State the units. Measure an expandable case as you will actually use it, not with its expansion zipped shut if you plan to pack more.

For a stroller, measure it folded for transport and mention any parts you plan to detach. For equipment that cannot fold, give its transport dimensions and describe any handling restriction. You can include the manufacturer's model link, but explain whether the published dimensions describe the packed item, the body alone or the product unfolded.

A photograph of the items together can help explain shapes and proportions. It complements the measurements; it does not establish fit by itself. Keep readable luggage tags, addresses and travel documents out of any photo you send.

Confirm the seating and cargo arrangement together

Ask the provider to check your list against the seats that must remain available for your party. Do not assume a seat can be folded to make room when someone needs to sit there. Likewise, do not rely on carrying a bulky case on a passenger's lap as the solution.

If your party has child-restraint needs, discuss the required arrangement and who will supply the restraint before booking. If someone travels with mobility equipment, describe its transport dimensions and the boarding arrangements needed. Do not assume a particular vehicle or equipment is available until it is confirmed.

When space is uncertain, ask the provider for a suitable alternative and a revised quote. That might mean a different vehicle arrangement or separate vehicles, subject to availability. A larger class name alone is not confirmation that the particular load works.

A luggage brief you can copy

Airport ride luggage brief
Trip: [date, airport or pickup address, destination].
Passengers: [total, including children].
Seating or boarding requirements: [details to confirm].
Large cases: [count; outside dimensions of each size; units].
Cabin bags and personal items: [counts and relevant sizes].
Stroller or bulky equipment: [count; folded or transport dimensions; handling restrictions].
Return-trip differences: [extra bags, different travelers or none].
Please confirm the vehicle arrangement for this passenger and luggage list, and let us know if a different arrangement or quote is needed.

Example: a family reports two large cases and a stroller, then realizes it also has two cabin bags, three backpacks and a separate stroller accessory bag. The second list is the one the provider needs. This example illustrates how to describe the load; it does not mean that either list fits a particular SUV.

Recheck after packing and before the return ride

If the luggage list changes, update the provider and obtain acknowledgment before pickup. That includes an extra case, a larger stroller, a different passenger count or equipment added for the return journey. A reservation based on the original list should not be treated as confirmation of the new one.

Check your airline's baggage requirements separately. Confirmation for the car ride does not establish what the airline will accept, and an airline bag allowance does not establish vehicle fit.

For Koast airport transfers, include the luggage brief with your ride request. If you are arranging the trip for another person, use the passenger handoff checklist to ensure the traveler and booker are working from the same confirmed plan.
